CRESTING THE PASS — atop her mount at the ridge summit, reining to a halt as the hidden valley spreads below, checking the iron compass in her palm against the peaks to confirm this is the sanctuary marked in her grandmother's journal.

SQUEEZING THE PASSAGE — wedged sideways in a narrow crack between cliff faces, pack dragging behind her as she inches toward the sliver of daylight ahead, the only route that avoids the patrol roads through the occupied territory.

SETTING THE SNARE — strung between two birches on one knee, hands threading wire through a bent sapling trigger, placing the fifth trap along the perimeter before dark, knowing something has been circling her camp each midnight.

SOUNDING THE DEPTH — standing thigh-deep where the river ford should be, probing ahead with her walking staff as spring melt has transformed the crossing, measuring whether her mount can navigate the channel or if they must backtrack three days.

BRUSHING THE INSCRIPTION — standing on a stone dais in an overgrown temple courtyard, one hand sweeping away centuries of moss from carved letters, her other holding the rubbing-paper ready as she confirms the dynasty name her patron seeks.

LEADING THE BRIDGE SPAN — one hand gripping her mount's halter, the other trailing along the rope guide as she tests each swaying plank across the gorge, whispering calm as the wood creaks and her saddlebags scrape the side cables.

CLIMBING THE SPIRE — three-quarters up a crumbling tower wall, fingers jammed in mortar gaps as she reaches for the window ledge where the signal mirror must be planted before the supply ship rounds the headland at noon.

Fletcher'S REST — seated cross-legged on a flat boulder beside the trail, knife shaving a shaft smooth while three dozen arrows wait for fletching, her distant gaze tracking clouds to judge if she can finish before the weather turns.

SCANNING THE SEXTANT — standing in a moonlit clearing, brass instrument raised to sight between two peaks, calculating her position against star charts after the avalanche erased the last five miles of trail and all familiar landmarks.

LIFTING THE BEAM — both hands straining under a collapsed roof timber blocking the root cellar entrance, her shoulders burning as she wedges it aside enough to squeeze through and reach the seed vault before the lord's soldiers confiscate the stores.

DISMOUNTING THE SCREE — sliding down a loose stone slope on her heels in controlled descent, one hand trailing her mount's reins as they navigate the shortcut, the valley floor still a hundred feet below and sunset an hour away.

PRESSING THE HEARTWOOD — palm flat against an ancient oak's trunk, standing motionless with eyes closed as she reads the forest's alarm through root and branch, learning what disturbance sent the deer fleeing and the ravens silent.

UNROLLING THE CHARTER — kneeling on a sunlit hilltop spreading the stained parchment across a flat stone, one hand pinning the crackling vellum while the other traces boundaries, confirming the land grant includes the spring her people need to survive the drought.

TRACKING PAUSE — standing perfectly still mid-stride on a game trail, one hand raised to halt her wolf companion, reading the disturbed moss and snapped twig that means something large passed hours ago.
RITUAL CAST — arm extended at shoulder height toward a standing stone, silver focus spinning above her palm, her cloak whipping in the wind as the air shimmers between her and the ancient marker.
MOUNTED ASCENT — atop her bay gelding cresting a mountain pass, the reins loose in one hand, shading her eyes against the glare to count the watchtowers in the disputed borderlands spreading below.
SPELL CHANNEL — standing before a lightning-scarred oak, both palms pressed to its trunk, eyes closed, drawing on the residual charge that tingles up her arms and makes her hair drift weightless.

MOUNT INJURY — kneeling beside her lame horse at streamside, lifting the foreleg gently, fingers probing the hot swelling above the hoof while fifteen miles of trackless moor stretch behind and ahead.
MAP READING — seated on a flat boulder at a crossroads, unrolling an oil-cloth map weighted with stones at its corners, comparing inked landmarks to the three valleys visible from this height.

CLIFF TRAIL — walking a narrow ledge-path along canyon walls, one hand trailing along rock for balance, the other holding her walking staff extended over the drop, prayer flags snapping in updrafts below.

CASKET UNSEAL — standing at a stone altar, both hands gripping the edge of a lead-lined reliquary lid, muscles tensed mid-effort, her shadow thrown huge by candlelight across inscribed walls warning against this exact act.
MOUNTED LISTEN — sitting astride her still horse at forest edge, head turned sharply left, one hand raised to silence the bit-jingle, as drums echo from the valley she must cross before nightfall.

STANDING STONE APPROACH — striding across a moorland clearing toward a circle of megaliths at sunset, staff planted with each step, her wolfhound ranging ahead as shadows lengthen and the stones begin their rumored hum.

HAWK LAUNCH AT DAWN — standing atop wind-scored mesa, arm extended skyward as her hooded hawk launches from leather glove toward distant canyon where smoke rises, carrying her message-scroll toward allies three days' ride south.
